title: Bell tests for collider decay processes
authors: Danilo M. Fucci, Alexandre C. Orthey, Alan J. Barr, Christopher G. Timpson
abstract: We propose Bell tests for collider decays using independently sampled analysis axes as settings and detector regions to assign binary or null outcomes. We show that a Bell violation requires postselection, opening a loophole. However, under measurement independence and operational equivalence of acceptance events across settings, any local model exploiting the loophole must be nonclassical in the sense of measurement contextuality. We derive a Bell inequality violated by singlet correlations when the effective spin-analyzing powers are sufficiently high. Its violation then witnesses Bell nonlocality or measurement contextuality.
summary: This work proposes a method to perform Bell tests using particle decay products from colliders, circumventing standard loopholes by focusing on joint acceptance events. It derives a Bell inequality whose violation proves either quantum nonlocality or measurement contextuality, provided certain operational equivalences hold true.
main_problem: The paper develops a theoretical framework to formulate and analyze Bell tests applicable to particle physics processes observed at colliders, specifically addressing loopholes introduced by detector acceptance.
main_result: A violation of a derived continuous-input Bell inequality, under assumptions of measurement independence and operational equivalence, witnesses either Bell nonlocality or joint-acceptance contextuality.
method: The methodology involves deriving local hidden-variable bounds for correlations measured from joint acceptance events and comparing these bounds to quantum mechanical predictions.
model_or_system: The system models the decay of parent qubits into daughter particles whose momenta act as spin analyzers, utilizing joint angular probability densities derived from collider decay kinematics.
key_observables: The Bell functional $B = -\mathbb{E}[\hat{x} \cdot \hat{y} a b]$, the effective spin-analyzing power ($\eta$), and the joint acceptance event rate ($N_D$).
important_parameters: The continuous input settings $\hat{x}, \hat{y} \in S^2$, and the optimal coarse-graining width ($\phi_{opt}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis critically assumes measurement independence and the operational equivalence of local and joint-acceptance events across all measurement settings.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometric coarse-graining defined by the analysis axis $\hat{x}$, showing the antipodal caps for outcomes $+1$ and $-1$, and the no-click outcome $\emptyset$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the difficulty of Bell testing in colliders to deriving the necessary conditions (operational equivalence) to close loopholes, culminating in the derivation and analysis of the continuous-input Bell inequality.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics, the rigorous mathematical framework for closing loopholes via operational equivalence and contextuality is highly relevant to foundational quantum information theory and quantum measurement theory.
